processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Samples synthesized by melting and casting in a vacuum-induction melting (VIM) furnace under 400 mbar Ar pressure; five Cu molds successively filled from a 4-kg ingot, and after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10 × 50 × 130 mm³-sized blocks were hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets were reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, and cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments (2 × 60 × 55 mm³) for each alloy composition.
Homogenization performed at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching (parent process proc_homog-1100c-2h-wq).
Aging conducted in air at 600 °C for 24 h, followed by oil quenching (the specific process state of this sample).

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic (fcc) microstructure with a grain size of ~20 μm and some retained Mn microsegregations (hot-rolled and water-quenched state).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Averages of three measurements for every material state; samples prepared by package spark erosion.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: aging response: the 6 wt.% Al variant does not show the pronounced aging strengthening observed for the 8 wt.% Al variant, nor the weakening/embrittlement of the Al-free alloy
tensile behavior: intermediate 2–6 wt.% Al variants (including 6Al) show a much smaller influence of aging than the ~8 wt.% Al variant

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements per material state
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)
characterization_methods.key_findings: 6 wt.% Al intermediate variant is only weakly affected by the 600 °C/24 h aging treatment.
Hardness is nearly flat around 200 HBW over 0–6 wt.% Al.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques; cross-sections in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials; hot rolling + water quenching gave a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size and retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: The 6 wt.% Al variant is an intermediate Al content of the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl RAP set and is only very weakly affected by the applied aging treatments in terms of mechanical data, compared with the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy (weakening/embrittlement) and Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al (strengthening) (b0024).

For the 30 wt.% Mn system, high amounts of Al (~8 wt.%) result in pronounced strengthening during aging attributed to nm-sized κ-carbides; the intermediate 2–6 wt.% Al variants do not show equivalent mechanical properties and show a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior (b0025).

Figure 5 (APT + TEM κ-carbide analysis after 24 h at 600 °C) is explicitly stated to be for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al low-density steel, not for the 6 wt.% Al sample; therefore its κ-carbide rod/platelet observations are excluded from this 6Al sample (b0034, figure_005).
Reference (Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C) as-homogenized mechanical values reported as context: 360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE (b0023).

General density trend from Fig. 1: mass density falls from roughly the 7.15 g/cm³ level near 6 wt.% Al to ~6.4 g/cm³ near 13 wt.% Al; this is a general Fe-Mn-Al-C trend, not a sample-specific measurement for Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al (figure_001).
